strengths.home: Winless at home in eight games under coach Lilian Popescu (no clean sheet at any venue in his tenure), one win since November 2024, and just beaten 4-0 by Slovakia. No major injuries; holds the head-to-head edge over Kazakhstan.
strengths.away: Kazakhstan: six games without a win (D3, L3), coming off a 2-2 draw with the Faroes in which both sides finished with ten men, and lost five of their last six UNL away trips. Missing Dastan Satpaev (injury) and Serhiy Malyi (suspended).

0ztMGL7s.synopsis: A scrappy three-way fight for second place between two sides in poor form. Neither looks dominant, and Flashscore's writer leans towards both teams scoring on scoring trends rather than any winning form.

strengths.home: Bulgaria: first win of the campaign came last time (2-0 against bottom side Luxembourg) but only one win in their last eight home UEFA games, under caretaker coach Atanas Ribarski after a 3-0 loss in Iceland. Atanas Iliev has scored seven in six; Martin Minchev is out.
strengths.away: Iceland: group leaders with a +6 goal difference, yet to concede away from home this cycle, and a draw could be enough to keep top spot. Andri Guðjohnsen has seven goals in seven for his club; Mikael Anderson is injured.

EHIYsb6t.synopsis: Iceland are warm favourites and the form points to an Icelandic win, with Bulgaria needing a result to stay alive. Flashscore's writer suggests backing against both teams scoring as an alternative angle in a likely one-sided game.

strengths.home: Netherlands: unbeaten in the group (W2, D2), one defeat in their last nine, 2+ goals in seven of those nine and ten competitive home games unbeaten. Virgil van Dijk has withdrawn injured; Tijjani Reijnders scored a late equaliser in the reverse fixture.
strengths.away: Greece: first League A campaign, unbeaten (W2, D2) with just three goals conceded, six wins in their last nine away internationals and five clean sheets in those games. Squad close to full strength; Fotis Ioannidis scored and assisted in the reverse fixture.

GzS4tf1n.synopsis: A group decider between two unbeaten sides locked on eight points, with the Dutch attack against a tight Greek defence. Flashscore's writer leans to a draw with both teams scoring, given the high-scoring Dutch matches and neither side losing yet.

strengths.home: Scotland: must win to keep promotion alive but have one win in six since the World Cup opener, lost both UNL games at Hampden and gave up a half-time lead to lose 2-1 in Slovenia. John McGinn scored in the reverse fixture; Scott McKenna is out.
strengths.away: North Macedonia: bottom of the group with four defeats and no goals in the cycle, winless in 12 and without a goal in 2026, with an eight-match winless away run. Darko Churlinov returns; Bojan Miovski left out.

KAogLGHG.synopsis: Scotland should have the edge on quality, but both sides are in poor form and the visitors cannot score. Flashscore's writer calls under 2.5 goals the obvious choice.

strengths.home: Serbia: bottom of the group (four defeats), six straight defeats in 2026 after missing the World Cup, only one win in eight, and Dušan Vlahović has withdrawn. Aleksandar Mitrović has scored six of his last eight goals after half-time.
strengths.away: Germany: under Jürgen Klopp a mixed run (W1, D2, L1) with just five goals in four games, but unbeaten in their last nine UNL away games (W2, D7) and they could still be relegated with a defeat. Jamal Musiala is injured and Karim Adeyemi left out.

6sjuQYG5.synopsis: Germany are the stronger side on paper but have been drawing a lot on the road and scoring little, while Serbia are in a deep slump. Flashscore's writer thinks another away draw for Germany would not be a surprise.

strengths.home: Slovenia: already second in the group on head-to-head, beat Scotland 2-1 last time and have lost once in their last eight UNL games (W4, D3). Without Benjamin Šeško and Timi Elšnik.
strengths.away: Switzerland: group leaders, four straight wins and a win would secure promotion (even a draw puts it in reach); unbeaten in opposition territory since relegation from League A (W4, D4). Breel Embolo returns; Granit Xhaka has withdrawn and Rubén Vargas and Ricardo Rodríguez are doubtful.

zqsNLPOQ.synopsis: Switzerland look the classier side, with Slovenia secure in second place and able to play without pressure. Flashscore's writer expects a strong Slovenian fight and backs Switzerland to win by a single goal.

strengths.home: Andorra: one win in 21 matches (D5, L15) and victory in only two of 25 UNL games; drew the reverse fixture 0-0. Eric Izquierdo is suspended; Guillaume López has scored both his goals at home.
strengths.away: Gibraltar: unbeaten in six games under Scott Wiseman (W3, D3), drew 1-1 in Malta last time and are on a ten-game unbeaten sequence. Captain Graeme Torrilla is suspended; Dan Bent scored the winner in the 2024 meeting.

dQZgSiJ5.synopsis: Two of the weakest sides in the competition, both chasing a first win in the tier, with Andorra the nominal favourites. Flashscore's writer points to a goalless first half, since a lack of goals has hurt both teams recently.

strengths.home: Liechtenstein: promoted whatever happens, but six games without scoring (five defeats, all 2-0) and eight straight home internationals without a goal. Captain Nicolas Hasler is out injured; Emanuel Zünd was the last scorer.
strengths.away: Azerbaijan: unbeaten leaders (W1, D2) who can take top spot with a win, though they have not won a competitive away game since October 2023. Abdulakh Khaybulaev scored the winner against Lithuania and has scored before the break each time in six goals.

K0OYkbnR.synopsis: Azerbaijan are the clear favourites against a side that cannot score, but neither team is prolific. Flashscore's writer suggests under 2.5 goals.

strengths.home: Luxembourg: bottom of the group after three straight defeats without scoring since opening with a win over Bulgaria, and at risk of a fourth home loss in a row. Coach Jeff Strasser's sides have won 13 of 14 when scoring first; Seid Korać is injured.
strengths.away: Estonia: second, unbeaten in their first four matches (W1, D3), five clean sheets in their last six games and a first possible promotion to League B. Winless in their last five UNL away games (D3, L2); Henri Anier is injured.

GIt89MIO.synopsis: Estonia look solid defensively against a struggling Luxembourg, though their weak away record tempers expectations. Flashscore's writer suggests a narrow 1-0 away win.

strengths.home: Slovakia: unbeaten in five home games, group leaders and a draw confirms promotion, with Vladimír Weiss able to rotate afterwards. Without Martin Dúbravka and Stanislav Lobotka (injury concerns); Dávid Hancko has scored late in two of his last three internationals.
strengths.away: Faroe Islands: drew all four group games, lost one of their last eight (W3, D4) and one of their last five away games, and still have an outside chance of the group. Martin Agnarsson is suspended; Géza Dávid Turi is in scoring form.

6XrUEaxf.synopsis: Slovakia are close to promotion and favoured at home, but the Faroes have been hard to beat and every one of their four group games has been a score draw. Flashscore's writer backs both teams to score.
